A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same HeurekaBench research work, with all 33 pages and Appendices A–I available. Text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that the scientific content matches; differences concern publication headers, affiliations, and first-page layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original pipeline evaluations, single-cell agent comparisons, component ablations, and human/LLM judge agreement studies in Section 4, with further empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the agent evaluations and ablations in Section 4 and supplementary comparisons in Appendices C, D, and H.

M1.justification: The insight extraction, code matching and generation, question filtering, and atomic-fact evaluation procedures are identical in Section 3 and Appendices A–B. No method component or agent procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both retain the same single-cell datasets and questions, including sc-HeurekaBench, Lite, and ToolUsage coverage. The FlyBase, BixBench, InsightBench, and BaisBench evaluations also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains BixBench-Agent, CellVoyager, and Biomni; Table 2 retains the same planner LLMs. The BaisBench comparison and baseline-versus-agent comparison in Appendices C.5 and H are also identical.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including the 750 MB cutoff for Lite, model configurations, correctness and MCQ metrics, and judge-study samples. No protocol is added or revised in the appendices.

E4.justification: The planner, critic-placement, and retriever ablations in Section 4.3 are unchanged. Judge-alignment studies, task-category analyses, and the manual failure analysis in Appendix D are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same three-run reporting and uncertainty notation. Human-rating aggregation, Spearman correlations, and Cohen’s kappa reporting in Section 4.3.1 and Appendix D.4 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported values and findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains correctness scores of 2.58 ± 0.05 for Claude-4-Sonnet and 2.08 ± 0.05 for GPT-OSS-120B; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The (D, Q, A) task formalization in Section 3.1 and associated definitions are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theoretical results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claim scope: validated benchmark construction, open-ended evaluation, and agent-design findings, including the stated critic benefit of up to 22%.

C2.justification: Interpretations of critic placement and model-dependent benefits are identical. The final-response-only evaluation limitation, insight-validation boundaries, and agent failure explanations in Section 5 and Appendices C–D are unchanged.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement and code-access link are identical. Generation, evaluation, and task prompts, along with data-collection and validation instructions in the appendices, contain no added or revised technical details.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and reference list are unchanged. Positioning relative to earlier benchmarks, including BaisBench in Appendix C.5, is identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header, numbered author affiliations and an ETH Zurich affiliation, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added running conference header and expanded affiliation block produce limited layout changes, including shifts on the first page. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–7 are unchanged; rendered page bodies on pages 2–33 are pixel-identical after excluding the header.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication and affiliation information with minor layout adjustments. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
